body:
Could you maybe add a more specific reference to the equation you are talking about?

I am assuming you mean slide 37+ from [here](https://gpuopen.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/GdcVdrLottes.pdf), but I am not sure if someone who hasn't read that presentation before would find it. If that is indeed the function you mean just adding the presentation's name and slide numbers would help a lot imo.

I take it this change is to fix potential problems the other tonemappers experience?

At some point in the future it would be nice if we hacked AGX to allow adjusting the white value as well, but that is out of scope of this PR.

This change is not necessary for this PR, but other tonemappers like ACES do not behave correctly with 0.0 white parameter. Since this PR is working on tonemappers, I figured it's as good of a time as any to address this.

A future PR that I will be making in the upcoming weeks will introduce white parameter support for AgX.

Hmm, yes, some more documentation could be useful. The source for generating these values is here, which is in the repository that is linked from the opening comments of the AgX tonemapper function: https://github.com/allenwp/AgX-GLSL-Shaders/blob/main/EaryChow-AgX/Mathematica/earychow-agx-simplified-approx.nb.txt

Linking the original slides or GDC talk would be a good addition...

Thanks for the review!

body:
```suggestion
			Uses a film-like tonemapping curve and desaturates bright values for a more realistic appearance. Better than other tonemappers at maintaining the hue of colors as they become brighter. Slightly slower than [constant TONE_MAPPER_FILMIC] and similar performance to [constant TONE_MAPPER_ACES].
```
